metaData.originalTitle: 【第 3697 期】Claude Code 自动记忆功能详解：告别重复交代，让 AI 记住你的项目
metaData.title: [Issue 3697] Claude Code Auto-Memory Feature Explained: Say Goodbye to Repeated Instructions, Let AI Remember Your Project
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides a detailed explanation of Claude Code's auto-memory feature, including how MEMORY.md works, its differences from CLAUDE.md, the memory hierarchy mechanism, and a practical demonstration of how to configure and control this feature.
metaData.summary: Addressing the pain point of having to repeatedly provide project context every time a new session is started in Claude Code, this article details the auto-memory feature launched by Anthropic. The core of this feature is the introduction of a MEMORY.md file, which is automatically created and maintained by Claude. Unlike the user-written CLAUDE.md, MEMORY.md is a project context record autonomously built by Claude during collaboration, covering aspects such as build commands, coding preferences, and architectural decisions. The article delves into the working mechanism of auto-memory, including the storage location (~/.claude/projects/<project>/memory/), the 200-line limit, and the memory hierarchy (user-level, project-level, auto-memory). Through a practical demonstration of creating a RAG pipeline, it showcases the complete workflow from enabling the feature to testing with a cold-start session. Finally, the article provides various methods to control auto-memory, including disabling it for individual projects, globally, and in CI environments.

mainPoints.point: Claude Code's auto-memory feature achieves cross-session context persistence through the MEMORY.md file.
mainPoints.explanation: This feature allows Claude to autonomously create and maintain MEMORY.md, recording project patterns, debugging insights, architectural notes, and personal preferences without manual user intervention, solving the pain point of needing to repeat context in each new session.

mainPoints.point: MEMORY.md and CLAUDE.md have a clear division of labor: instructions vs. memos.
mainPoints.explanation: CLAUDE.md is a user-written instruction file that tells Claude how to behave; MEMORY.md is an auto-generated memo by Claude that records the context accumulated during collaboration. The two work together to provide more comprehensive initial session context.

mainPoints.point: The auto-memory feature offers multiple control methods to suit different scenario needs.
mainPoints.explanation: Users can enable or disable this feature via the /memory command, the settings.json configuration file, or the environment variable CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY, allowing fine-grained control at the project level, global level, and in CI environments.

keyQuotes: You no longer have to worry about losing session context in Claude Code. The new auto-memory feature solves one of the most frustrating problems in the workflow.
CLAUDE.md is your instructions, while MEMORY.md is Claude's own memo.
The auto-memory feature is enabled by default after you update Claude Code, requiring no additional installation or configuration — it works out of the box.
Claude autonomously determines which information is important and records it automatically.

If you're about to do some exploratory work that you don't want Claude to remember, or just running a one-off task temporarily, this is the quickest way to pause the current project's memory function.
